snapshot.what_it_does: Larsen & Toubro is a diversified engineering, construction and manufacturing conglomerate that executes large, complex projects and manufactures engineered-to-order equipment, alongside technology, financial services and realty businesses. It positions itself as a tech-driven solutions provider, using digitalisation, AI and IoT across its project life-cycle.

segments.name: Infrastructure & Utilities (Infrastructure Projects)
segments.share: not stated (FY2025-26 revenue ₹79,785 crore; 57% of order book; 46% of order inflow)
segments.note: Largest contributor; spans Buildings & Factories, Transportation Infrastructure, Heavy Civil, Power Transmission & Distribution, Water & Effluent Treatment, Minerals & Metals (p35, p44, p45)

segments.name: Energy - Conventional
segments.share: not stated (Energy Projects segment revenue ₹54,889 crore)
segments.note: Hydrocarbon Onshore & Offshore and CarbonLite Solutions; order inflows ₹1,36,921 crore, up 56.4%; 74% international revenue; OPM declined to 6.8% (p35, p84)

segments.name: Energy - Green
segments.note: Renewable energy infrastructure including solar, onshore and offshore wind (p35)

segments.name: Hi-Tech Manufacturing
segments.note: Heavy Engineering and Precision Engineering & Systems; OPM 16.7% (p35, p95, p96)

segments.name: Technology, Platforms & Services
segments.share: not stated (IT & Technology Services revenue ₹28,353 crore)
segments.note: IT services (LTM), Engineering R&D (LTTS), B2B e-commerce (L&T-SuFin), skilling (L&T EduTech), data centers/cloud (Larsen & Toubro Vyoma), semiconductor chip design (LTSCT) (p35, p45)

segments.name: Financial Services
segments.note: L&T Finance Limited, retail lending NBFC (p35, p45)

segments.name: Realty
segments.note: Residential and commercial real estate development (p35)

segments.note: Focus on production of green hydrogen and its derivatives (p35, p45)

snapshot.geographies: Operations span multiple geographies; international revenue was 54% of Group revenue in FY2025-26 (vs 50% prior year) and international orders 52% of the order book, with a large chunk of order wins from GCC countries (p10, p44).
key_facts: Group Revenue of ₹2.86 lakh crore in FY2025-26, up 12% y-o-y (p10)
Record Order Book of ₹7.40 lakh crore, up 28% y-o-y; international orders 52% (p10)
Recurring PAT of ₹17,238 crore, up 18% y-o-y (p10)
Group Net Debt:Equity improved to 0.35:1 in FY2025-26 from 0.6:1 (p10)
Recommended final dividend of ₹38 per share for FY2025-26 (p11)

promised_vs_delivered.verdict: Mixed credibility: management beat its FY26 order inflow guidance and gave accurate directional margin warnings, but missed its headline FY26 revenue (12% vs 15%), P&M margin (8.5% target) and ROE (15.5% vs 18%) commitments. To its credit, management explicitly acknowledged the revenue and margin misses on the Q4 FY26 call rather than obscuring them.

bull.point: Record ₹7.40 lakh crore order book, up 28% YoY with 52% international orders, gives strong multi-year execution visibility.
FY26 delivered ₹2.86 lakh crore revenue (+12%), recurring PAT ₹17,238 crore (+18%), and net debt/equity improved to 0.35:1 from 0.6:1.
FY27 started with order inflows of ₹1,080 billion, up 14% YoY, while Q1 revenue rose 7% and PAT rose 14%.
bull.cite: Q1 FY27 call p.4, p.6; quarterly_actuals 2026-06-30

bear.point: Management missed FY26 revenue (12% vs 15%), P&M margin (7.8% vs 8.5%) and ROE (15.5% vs 18%) commitments.
bear.cite: Q4 FY26 call p.5, p.7, p.13

bear.point: Margins remain pressured: Energy margin fell to 6.5% vs 8.2%, PPM margin was 7.0% in Q1 FY27, and latest quarterly operating margin is 7.3%.
bear.cite: Q4 FY26 call p.8; Q1 FY27 call p.6; quarterly_actuals 2026-09-30

bear.point: Execution risk is visible: ₹50 billion Q4 revenue lost to Middle East supply-chain issues, Kuwait $4.5 billion tenders cancelled, divestments slipped.
bear.cite: Q4 FY26 call p.14; Q3 FY26 call p.9; Q4 FY26 call p.4

watch: Whether FY27 revenue stays within 10-12% guidance after the flagged soft first half.
P&M and Energy margin recovery toward the missed 8.5% FY26 P&M target.
Closure of Nabha Power and Hyderabad Metro divestments, plus Kuwait re-tender awards during calendar 2026.
